scope: Run 37: 1952 Pusan crisis command-chain, cabinet resistance, compromise and UN provenance follow-up

documents.title: Lightner telegram 1170: Van Fleet-Rhee discussion of martial law command
documents.author: E. Allan Lightner Jr.
documents.organization: U.S. Embassy Pusan / Department of State
documents.notes: Van Fleet stated neither he nor ROK Army Chief of Staff had been consulted before martial law. Rhee said cabinet had decided martial law, he approved it and suggested including Pusan, then telephoned Gen. Lee; Defense Minister would issue decree, Won Yong-dok would be martial-law commander and take orders directly from President. This is a contemporaneous U.S. diplomatic report of Rhee's own account, not the missing Korean decree/order.

documents.title: Johnson memorandum: issues requiring decision in Korean political crisis
documents.author: U. Alexis Johnson
documents.notes: Separates immediate U.S. concerns: release of legislators, end coercion, normal Assembly functioning and lifting martial law; also records contemplated intervention measures. U.S. policy judgment is not treated as Korean legal finding.

documents.title: Lightner telegram 1259: Chang Taik-sang cabinet account and compromise draft
documents.author: E. Allan Lightner Jr.
documents.organization: U.S. Embassy Pusan / Department of State
documents.provenance: official U.S. diplomatic record reporting Prime Minister Chang's account
documents.notes: Chang reported most cabinet members refused to endorse dissolution; Lee Bum-suk proposed arresting all Assemblymen; Rhee ordered Lee not to stop demonstrators entering Pusan. Chang described a compromise draft with direct presidential election, Assembly-confirmed PM, two-thirds no-confidence and Assembly confirmation of ministers. Preserve as Chang's reported account pending Korean cabinet minutes.

documents.title: Acheson telegram 907: U.S. instruction favoring legal-framework compromise
documents.author: Dean Acheson
documents.provenance: official U.S. diplomatic instruction cleared by Truman
documents.notes: Washington preferred means short of military intervention, saw Rhee remaining president under controls as potentially serving U.S.-UN interests, and cited the Prime Minister's proposal as an example of compromise within the constitutional framework.

documents.title: Lightner assessment of Rhee, cabinet administration and Lee Bum-suk group
documents.author: E. Allan Lightner Jr.
documents.organization: U.S. Embassy Pusan / Department of State
documents.notes: Embassy assessment argues cabinet and lower officials were highly centralized around presidential referral and identifies Lee Bum-suk as central to a coercive inner group. Store strictly as observer assessment, useful for testing administrative-centralization claims rather than as self-proving fact.

documents.title: Rhee letter to Truman on political disturbance
documents.author: Syngman Rhee
documents.organization: ROK Presidency / U.S. official documentary edition
documents.provenance: presidential correspondence in official U.S. documentary edition
documents.notes: Rhee characterizes government action as law-and-order enforcement and invokes petitions, provincial legislatures and popular demand for Assembly dissolution, while saying he still seeks a solution without dissolution. Adversarial first-party account.

documents.title: Hickerson memorandum: continuing political crisis
documents.author: John D. Hickerson
documents.notes: Argues a compromise forced under martial law/threats would not restore constitutional government and proposes possible last-resort UNC action. This records U.S. policy advocacy, not a Korean judicial determination.

documents.title: Muccio telegram 1395: intervention thresholds and actor risks
documents.author: John J. Muccio
documents.organization: U.S. Embassy Pusan / Department of State
documents.notes: Muccio lists intervention triggers including dissolution, mass arrests, interference with ROK Army, violence, and a possible Lee Bum-suk takeover using police/youth corps. This is contingency assessment, not evidence that the contemplated takeover occurred.

documents.title: Muccio telegram 1470: compromise and intervention timing
documents.author: John J. Muccio
documents.organization: U.S. Embassy Pusan / Department of State
documents.notes: Muccio judged an immediate ultimatum undesirable while a compromise leaving Rhee in office with restrictions and restoring Assembly independence still appeared possible.

documents.title: Muccio telegram 1471: post-crisis consequences assessment
documents.author: John J. Muccio
documents.organization: U.S. Embassy Pusan / Department of State
documents.notes: Warns that a Rhee victory while martial law and trials continued would damage legitimacy, aid support and moderate participation. Observer forecast retained separately from event facts.

documents.title: FRUS editorial note on guided escort, July 4 vote and implementing legislation
documents.organization: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian
documents.provenance: official U.S. documentary edition summarizing UN A/2187 pp.9-11
documents.notes: Records July 2 government announcement that absent legislators would be guided and escorted by police; July 4 plenary 166 members, 163-0 with 3 abstentions; July 15 implementing legislation; points directly to A/2187 pp.9-11.

documents.title: Report of the United Nations Commission for the Unification and Rehabilitation of Korea, GAOR 7th Session Supplement No.14 (A/2187)
documents.provenance: official UN report identified through UN Digital Library records and FRUS citations
documents.notes: Exact report identity and use in 1952 First Committee records verified; full report text was not directly retrievable in this run. FRUS d149 cites pp.12-17 for the May 28 statement; FRUS d206 cites pp.9-11 for July events. Keep originalObtained=false until full item is opened.

documents.title: First Committee 516th meeting official record
documents.notes: Confirms A/2187 was before the committee and that delegates explicitly debated use of its account of May-July political events in the Republic of Korea.

documents.title: Yearbook of the United Nations 1952, Political and Security Questions: Korea
documents.notes: Confirms A/1881 and A/2187 were reports before the General Assembly/First Committee during the seventh session; useful independent provenance for UNCURK report chain.

openTargets: ROK martial-law proclamation/decree and Defense Ministry issuance
Won Yong-dok appointment/order and command logs
June 3 Korean cabinet minutes corroborating Chang account
